The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Missing test changes or validation evidence

adjudication.rationale: The diff includes substantial new automated test coverage: new specs for TopicRetriever, EmbedController, Jobs::PollFeed, and TopicEmbed. TopicEmbed spec even asserts the new cook_method/raw_html behavior. While not every small change (e.g., PostRevisor validate option) has an explicit test, the proposed finding is vague and not a clearly verifiable defect in this diff, since tests/validation evidence were in fact added.

adjudication_records.issue_text: XSS/injection in TopicEmbed.import from unescaped url interpolated into HTML cooked with raw_html
Modifying existing migration create_top_topics.rb to add force: true risks silently destroying data in environments where it already ran

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes an already-existing migration to `create_table :top_topics, force: true`. While `force: true` will drop an existing table if the migration is executed, migrations that have already run in an environment are not re-executed on subsequent `db:migrate`, so this change does not “silently destroy data” in environments where the migration already ran. Additionally, if the migration were rolled back and re-run, the rollback of a `create_table` migration would already drop the table (losing data) regardless of `force: true`. Any data-loss scenario would require atypical/incorrect migration state (e.g., table exists but migration not recorded), which is speculative beyond the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: create_topic_embeds.rb uses force: true, destroying existing topic_embeds data if migration runs where table exists

adjudication.rationale: In `db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb`, the migration calls `create_table :topic_embeds, force: true`. In Rails, `force: true` will drop the existing table before creating it, which would destroy any existing `topic_embeds` data if this migration is executed in an environment where the table already exists (e.g., an out-of-sync DB or a manually re-run migration). This behavior is directly present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PollFeed assumes every RSS item has a content element (i.content.scrub), causing NoMethodError if missing
SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) in PollFeed has no error handling for network failures, failing silently due to retry: false

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, `rss = SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` performs a network request via `open-uri` with no `begin/rescue` around it. Any network/DNS/timeout/parsing exception will bubble up and cause the job to error. Since the job sets `sidekiq_options retry: false`, these transient failures will not be retried automatically. The only inaccurate part of the finding is "failing silently"—it will raise/fail rather than silently succeed—but the core issue (no error handling combined with no retries) is directly present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Removing --category option from disqus.thor breaks Disqus import categorization functionality without a replacement

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the Thor CLI flag `method_option :category, aliases: '-c'` and deletes the corresponding `category_id` lookup and passing `category: category_id` into `PostCreator.new(...)`. The new code path uses `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`, which does not accept or apply any category. So Disqus imports can no longer be targeted to a specified category via `--category`, and there is no alternative in this change to preserve that functionality.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Data fidelity regression in disqus.thor where original post dates are lost because TopicEmbed.import_remote/import don't accept created_at

adjudication.rationale: In lib/tasks/disqus.thor, the import path changed from creating the topic via `PostCreator.new(..., created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at]), ...)` to `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`. `TopicEmbed.import_remote` calls `TopicEmbed.import` which in turn calls `PostCreator.new` without any `created_at` option. Since `PostCreator` only sets `post.created_at` when `@opts[:created_at]` is present (see lib/post_creator.rb), the Disqus thread’s original `t[:created_at]` is no longer applied, so imported topics/posts will get the current time instead. This is a verifiable data fidelity regression introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed.js lacks defensive checks for undefined discourseUrl and discourseEmbedUrl globals, causing ReferenceError

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js`, the code directly reads `discourseUrl` and `discourseEmbedUrl` when building `iframe.src` (`iframe.src = discourseUrl + "embed/best?embed_url=" + encodeURIComponent(discourseEmbedUrl);`). In JavaScript, referencing an undeclared global identifier throws a `ReferenceError` at runtime. The file only has `/* global ... */` comments (lint hints) and contains no `typeof discourseUrl !== 'undefined'`/fallback checks, so if a page includes this script without defining those globals first, it will crash exactly as the finding describes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed.html.erb uses non-standard document['body'].offsetHeight instead of document.body.offsetHeight

adjudication.rationale: In app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb the code uses `document['body'].offsetHeight`. In JavaScript, bracket-notation property access (`document['body']`) is equivalent to dot notation (`document.body`) as long as the property exists, which it does in browsers that support `document.body`. This is not a correctness defect introduced by the diff; at most it's a stylistic/readability preference, not a verifiable bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed/best.html.erb has no nil-guard for @topic_view, causing NoMethodError if topic is deleted

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, `@topic_view` is only used when `topic_id` is present, and in that branch it is always assigned via `@topic_view = TopicView.new(...)`. If `topic_id` is not present, the action renders `'loading'` instead (so `best.html.erb` is not rendered). Therefore, there is no verifiable path in this diff where `best.html.erb` would execute with `@topic_view == nil` and cause a `NoMethodError`. If the underlying topic were deleted, the more likely outcome would be `TopicView.new` raising (not `@topic_view` being nil), which is not something the view’s nil-guard would address and isn’t demonstrated in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed/best.html.erb assumes post.user is non-nil, causing NoMethodError for deleted users

adjudication.rationale: In the new `app/views/embed/best.html.erb`, the template does dereference `post.user` (`post.user.small_avatar_url`, `post.user.username`) without a nil-check. However, the diff provides no evidence that `TopicView` can yield posts with a missing associated user, and in typical Discourse behavior users are not hard-deleted in a way that leaves posts with `user_id` pointing to a non-existent row (deletion is generally soft/anonymized or reassigned). So the claimed NoMethodError for “deleted users” is speculative rather than a verifiable defect introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: <%= raw post.cooked %> in embed/best.html.erb renders RSS content without sanitization, creating an end-to-end XSS path

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The diff introduces a path where untrusted HTML can be rendered without Discourse’s normal cooking/sanitization. In `TopicEmbed.import`, imported feed/article contents are passed to `PostCreator` with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and `skip_validations: true`. `Post#cook` then returns `raw` directly when `cook_method` is `:raw_html`, bypassing the rendering pipeline. In `app/views/embed/best.html.erb`, the template outputs this with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, which will emit the imported HTML verbatim. For the RSS polling path (`Jobs::PollFeed`), `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` is not sanitized/filtered, so a malicious feed entry containing `<script>`/event-handler attributes/etc. would be stored and then rendered, creating an end-to-end XSS vector in the embed page.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed_controller.rb params.require(:embed_url) raises 400 Bad Request, not 404 as test comment claims, and tests don't verify the response code

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, `params.require(:embed_url)` will raise `ActionController::ParameterMissing` if the param is absent, but the diff does not show how that exception is mapped to an HTTP status in this app (it could be rescued globally). Also, the first spec (`it "is 404 without an embed_url"`) does not actually assert `404`; it only checks `response.should_not be_success`, and it may not even reach `params.require` because `ensure_embeddable` runs first and can raise before the action body (e.g., if `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`/referer checks fail). So the finding is primarily about a misleading test description / not asserting status, not a clearly verifiable functional defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No rate limiting on /embed/best endpoint, allowing abuse by repeatedly triggering retrieve_topic jobs

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, when no existing embed is found it unconditionally enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` on every request. There is no per-IP/user/request throttling or deduplication before enqueuing. Although `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?` throttles the *work* (via a Redis key expiring in 60s per `embed_url`), the job is still created and will run, so a client can spam `/embed/best?embed_url=...` and flood Sidekiq with `retrieve_topic` jobs that mostly no-op. The `ensure_embeddable` check relies on the `Referer` header (client-controlled), so it doesn’t prevent this abuse by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve calls PollFeed.execute synchronously inside a Sidekiq job, blocking the worker thread

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `lib/topic_retriever.rb`, `perform_retrieve` directly calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true. This is a synchronous invocation (not enqueued via Sidekiq), and `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` performs network I/O (`open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)`) and iterates/imports items. When `TopicRetriever#retrieve` is run from the Sidekiq job `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` (`app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb`), that worker thread will be occupied while the feed poll runs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicRetriever#fetch_http silently returns if embed_by_username doesn't exist, leaving embed stuck on Loading... without errors or logs

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicRetriever#fetch_http`, the code looks up `User.where(username_lower: SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase).first` and then `return if user.blank?` without raising, rendering an error, or logging. In `EmbedController#best`, when `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed` returns nil, it enqueues retrieval and renders the `loading` template, which just reloads every 30s. If `SiteSetting.embed_by_username` is unset/empty or refers to a non-existent user, retrieval will repeatedly no-op and no `TopicEmbed` will ever be created, so the embed can remain stuck on “Loading...” with no visible error or log message attributable to this condition.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls fails to absolutize protocol-relative URLs (//) and relative URLs without a leading slash

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls`, links are only rewritten when `href.present? && href.start_with?('/')` (and similarly for `img` `src`). This means protocol-relative URLs like `//cdn.example.com/a.png` (which start with `//`) and other relative forms like `images/a.png`, `./images/a.png`, or `../a` will not be converted to absolute URLs, despite the method’s stated purpose “Convert any relative URLs to absolute.” This is directly verifiable from the diff and can result in embedded/imported content containing unresolved/broken URLs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls port-handling ignores scheme, incorrectly appending :80 for https or :443 for http

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls`, the code appends `:#{uri.port}` only when the port is neither 80 nor 443 (`if uri.port != 80 && uri.port != 443`). That means it will *not* append `:443` for `http://host:443` nor `:80` for `https://host:80`, even though those are non-default ports for those schemes. The proposed finding claims the opposite (that it incorrectly appends `:80` for https or `:443` for http), which is not what the diff does.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicEmbed.import silently fails if PostCreator#create returns a falsy post, committing transaction without raising an error

adjudication.rationale:
In TopicEmbed.import, the new-embed branch wraps creation in `Topic.transaction` but does not handle failure from `PostCreator#create`: 
```rb
post = creator.create
if post.present?
  TopicEmbed.create!(...)
end
```
If `creator.create` returns nil/false, the method just exits the transaction and returns `post` (nil) without raising/logging, so the import can fail silently. Because the transaction only rolls back on exceptions, any DB writes that `PostCreator#create` performed before returning falsy (if it can) would still be committed, potentially leaving inconsistent state. The code explicitly anticipates a non-present post, but does nothing in that case.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicEmbed.import_remote calls open(url).read with no timeout, size limit, or error handling, risking indefinite hang

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `TopicEmbed.import_remote` does `Readability::Document.new(open(url).read, ...)` with a plain `open(url)` call and no options (e.g., `open_timeout`, `read_timeout`) and no `rescue`/error handling. This means the network fetch can block the calling job/thread for an unbounded/very long time depending on runtime defaults and can also raise exceptions (timeouts, DNS errors, HTTP errors, huge responses) that are not handled here, causing the import/job to fail. There is also no size limit on the response body before `.read`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: loading.html.erb reload timer (30s) and discourse_expires_in (1m) mismatch causes stale loading pages to be cached, sticking users on Loading...

adjudication.rationale: EmbedController#best unconditionally calls `discourse_expires_in 1.minute` even when it renders `loading`. The loading page uses `setTimeout(... document.location.reload(), 30000)`. With a 60s cache lifetime, a reload at 30s can be satisfied from cache (same Loading HTML) rather than hitting the server to see whether the topic/embed is now available, delaying transition off the loading page until cache expiry. The exact caching behavior depends on how `discourse_expires_in` sets Cache-Control and how the client/proxy honors it, but the 30s reload vs 60s cache mismatch is a real, diff-visible defect risk.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed.js iframe height never shrinks when content becomes shorter, leaving visible whitespace

adjudication.rationale: In `embed.js`, the message handler unconditionally assigns `iframe.height = e.data.height + "px"` when it receives a `discourse-resize` message—there is no logic that only increases height or prevents shrinking. Therefore, if the embedded page posts a smaller `height`, the iframe will shrink accordingly. The diff’s embedded layout (`layouts/embed.html.erb`) posts a resize message on `window.onload` (and again on full reloads), so shrinking is not inherently blocked by the code shown. The finding claims it “never shrinks,” which is not verifiable from this diff and is contradicted by the assignment behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Gemfile adds ruby-readability and simple-rss without version constraints, risking breaking changes on bundle update

adjudication.rationale: While the Gemfile adds `ruby-readability` and `simple-rss` without explicit version constraints, the diff also updates `Gemfile_rails4.lock`, which pins them to specific versions (`ruby-readability (0.5.7)` and `simple-rss (1.3.1)`) along with their dependencies. In a Bundler-managed app, the lockfile is the primary mechanism preventing breaking changes on normal installs; “risk on bundle update” is a general, speculative concern that applies to most unconstrained gems and is not a concrete defect introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Trailing newline removed from migrate_word_counts.rb is an unrelated stylistic regression

adjudication.rationale: The diff for db/migrate/20131210181901_migrate_word_counts.rb shows the file now lacks a trailing newline ("\\ No newline at end of file") and only whitespace changes otherwise. This is a minor formatting/style regression, not a bug, security issue, or functional defect introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: retrieve_topic.rb user_id argument is dead code that doesn't affect topic creation user, missing staff-throttle behavior test

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb`, `user_id` is not dead code: it is used to look up the user and pass `no_throttle: user.try(:staff?)` into `TopicRetriever`, which changes behavior by bypassing the 60-second throttle for staff (`retrieved_recently?` returns false when `@opts[:no_throttle]`). While it’s true that `user_id` does not affect which user creates the imported topic (that’s determined by `SiteSetting.embed_by_username` in `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` / `Jobs::PollFeed`), that does not make the parameter dead or defective. The “missing staff-throttle behavior test” is about test coverage, not a verifiable defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: site_settings.yml embed_by_username lacks validation that the user exists, without admin UI guidance or tests

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces the `embed_by_username` site setting and uses it in `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` and `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` to look up a user (`User.where(username_lower: ...).first`). If the user does not exist, both paths explicitly `return if user.blank?`, so the system fails safely by skipping import rather than raising or misbehaving. The proposed finding is mainly about UX/validation/test coverage (no enforcement that the username corresponds to an existing user), but this is not a clear correctness/security defect introduced by the diff, and the behavior is already guarded in code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_embed_spec.rb lacks tests for TopicEmbed.import_remote network fetch code path

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `TopicEmbed.import_remote` (which does an `open(url).read` and uses `ruby-readability`), and the new `spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb` only exercises `.import` (creation/update, URL absolutizing) and does not cover `.import_remote`. However, missing a test for a new code path is a test-coverage suggestion, not a verifiable bug/security/correctness defect introduced by the diff. Nothing in the diff indicates the code is failing due to this lack of coverage.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed_controller_spec.rb error tests only assert should_not be_success, missing assertions for specific error classes, response status, and X-Frame-Options header

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `embed_controller_spec.rb` with several “error” cases that only assert `response.should_not be_success`. That’s a test-strength/completeness observation, not a verifiable defect introduced by the production code in the diff. Nothing in the diff indicates the controller is returning the wrong status or wrong exception class; the spec’s lack of more specific assertions does not cause failing behavior or a correctness/security issue by itself. Also, the spec already asserts `X-Frame-Options == "ALLOWALL"` in the success context; omitting it in error cases is not clearly a bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed_controller.rb lacks tests verifying successful responses contain X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL in all success paths

adjudication.rationale: The diff already includes tests for this header. In `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb`, within the `context "success"` block, an `after` hook asserts `response.should be_success` and `response.headers['X-Frame-Options'].should == "ALLOWALL"`. That `after` runs for each success-path example, covering both cases where `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed` returns `nil` (enqueue/retrieve path) and where it returns a topic id (TopicView path).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unrelated whitespace change in db/migrate/20131210181901_migrate_word_counts.rb:4 removes trailing whitespace and drops final newline, which is scope drift unrelated to embed URL handling

adjudication.rationale: The diff does include a whitespace-only change in db/migrate/20131210181901_migrate_word_counts.rb (removing trailing whitespace on a blank line) and it also removes the final newline ("\\ No newline at end of file"). However, this is a style/formatting nit and minor scope drift, not a bug, security issue, or correctness defect introduced by the patch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dangerous force: true added to db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:3 will silently drop the top_topics table and its data if the migration is re-run

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes an existing migration to `create_table :top_topics, force: true`. In Rails, `force: true` will drop the table if it already exists before recreating it. If this migration is ever re-run against a DB where `top_topics` already exists (e.g., due to partial deployment, manual rerun, or unusual migration state), it can silently delete existing `top_topics` data.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Disqus import task (lib/tasks/disqus.thor:117) loses the --category/-c CLI option and related category_id logic when refactored to use TopicEmbed.import_remote, causing a behavior regression

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the Disqus Thor task option `method_option :category, aliases: '-c'` and deletes the `category_id` lookup/passing logic. Previously it would pass `category: category_id` into `PostCreator.new(...)`; now it calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])` with no category parameter, and there is no other code in this diff preserving `--category/-c` behavior. This is a clear, verifiable behavior change/regression for users relying on that CLI option.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EmbedController#best (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:11) only checks for presence of embed_url with params.require but does not validate it is a valid HTTP/HTTPS URL, allowing arbitrary strings to be enqueued into Jobs::RetrieveTopic

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, `embed_url = params.require(:embed_url)` only enforces presence and then unconditionally enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ..., embed_url: embed_url)` when no existing `TopicEmbed` is found. There is no controller-side validation that `embed_url` is a well-formed HTTP/HTTPS URL. While `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` later rejects invalid/other-host URLs (often making the job a no-op), the diff still introduces the behavior that arbitrary strings can be submitted to `/embed/best` (subject to the referer-host gate) and get enqueued into `Jobs::RetrieveTopic`, allowing unnecessary job queue growth/work.

adjudication_records.issue_text: poll_feed (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35) calls CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub) without handling nil i.content, causing NoMethodError when an RSS/Atom item lacks a content element

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, within rss.items.each, the code does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`. If `i.content` is nil (which is common for feeds that only provide `description`/`summary` and not `content`/`content:encoded`), calling `.scrub` on nil will raise `NoMethodError`. There is no nil-guard or fallback in the diff, so the failure is a real possibility introduced by this code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: absolutize_urls (app/models/topic_embed.rb:64-77) only converts paths starting with / to absolute URLs but does not handle protocol-relative URLs like //example.com/path, leaving them broken in imported content

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls`, the code intentionally rewrites only *root-relative* paths (`href`/`src` that `start_with?('/')`) to the source host prefix. A protocol-relative URL like `//example.com/path` is already a valid network-path reference in HTML and will resolve in browsers to the current page’s scheme; it is not inherently “broken” and also should not be rewritten to the source host prefix (it points to a different host). So the finding claims a defect that is not verifiably present from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: force: true in db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:4 will silently drop the topic_embeds table if it already exists, which is risky and unnecessary for a fresh table creation

adjudication.rationale: In the new migration `db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb`, the table is created with `create_table :topic_embeds, force: true`. In Rails, `force: true` will drop the table if it already exists before creating it. That behavior is real and can lead to silent data loss if the migration is re-run (or if the table already exists due to a partially applied/rolled-back state), and it is not necessary for a normal “create a fresh table” migration.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Missing validation for cook_method on Post model (app/models/post.rb:63-64) allows arbitrary integer values to be set via PostCreator since no validation ensures the stored value falls within the valid enum range
postMessage origin check in embed.js:19 uses substring matching (indexOf) instead of strict equality, allowing attacker origins like 'https://forum.example.co' to pass as 'https://forum.example.com'

adjudication.rationale: In app/assets/javascripts/embed.js, the message handler validates the sender with `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }`. This is substring/prefix matching, not an exact origin check. If `discourseUrl` is `https://forum.example.com/`, an event with `e.origin` of `https://forum.example.co` will yield `indexOf(...) === 0` and be accepted, allowing an unintended origin to trigger the resize logic. A strict origin comparison (e.g., comparing `new URL(discourseUrl).origin === e.origin`) is needed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: request.referer interpolated unescaped into JS string literal in embed.html.erb:10, allowing XSS breakout via crafted referer that passes host check
matched_golden_ids: An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same vulnerability: the unescaped request.referer header is interpolated into a JavaScript context/string, enabling XSS if an attacker supplies malicious referer content. Candidate adds location and notes host-check bypass but the core issue matches.

adjudication_records.issue_text: url interpolated directly into HTML in topic_embed.rb:14 without escaping, causing stored XSS in every imported post via unvalidated url parameter

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicEmbed.import`, it appends HTML containing `"#{url}"` directly into `contents` without escaping. The only validation is `return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, which does not prevent characters like `'` (or other HTML-breaking characters) from being included in `url`. Because imported posts are created with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and `Post#cook` returns `raw` for that method, the HTML is stored/rendered without the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline, and `embed/best.html.erb` renders it via `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. A crafted feed/link value could therefore inject stored XSS into imported posts.

adjudication_records.issue_text: raw post.cooked rendered with no sanitization in best.html.erb:16, allowing untrusted HTML to render raw for cook_method=raw_html (RSS imports)

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a `cook_method` enum with `:raw_html` and changes `Post#cook` to `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, explicitly bypassing the normal cooking/rendering pipeline (which is where Discourse typically sanitizes/filters HTML). `TopicEmbed.import` is used for RSS/Atom imports and passes `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` while using feed-provided `content` (`CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`) that is not sanitized in this diff. In `app/views/embed/best.html.erb`, it renders `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, so for `raw_html` posts `post.cooked == post.raw` and is output unescaped. This is a verifiable XSS/HTML injection risk if imported content contains unsafe HTML (e.g., script tags or event handlers).

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed_controller.rb:28 relies solely on Referer header as embedding gatekeeper which can be omitted/spoofed, with no signed-URL, origin allowlist, or rate-limit

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`, access is granted solely by comparing `URI(request.referer || '').host` to `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, and then it sets `X-Frame-Options = "ALLOWALL"`. The `Referer` header is optional and can be spoofed by non-browser clients, so this is a weak gatekeeper for an otherwise publicly reachable endpoint (`GET /embed/best`). There’s no signed token or other verifiable proof of embedding origin in the diff, and the controller can enqueue `:retrieve_topic` jobs when no embed exists, without any controller-level rate limit or auth beyond the spoofable referer check (the retriever throttles fetches, but not job enqueue volume).

adjudication_records.issue_text: open(url) in topic_embed.rb:37 and poll_feed.rb:31 uses Kernel#open against arbitrary URLs, permitting file://, pipe, and other non-HTTP schemes (SSRF/LFI) with no timeout or size cap
matched_golden_ids: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags PollFeed’s use of Kernel#open on a URL without validation, enabling SSRF (and even non-HTTP schemes like file://). This matches the golden issue of open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) allowing arbitrary internal/external fetches when the setting is attacker-controlled, though the candidate adds extra related concerns (other file + timeout/size).

adjudication_records.issue_text: No foreign-key constraints on topic_id or post_id in create_topic_embeds.rb, leaving dangling rows when Topic or Post is deleted

adjudication.rationale: The new migration `20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb` creates `topic_embeds` with `topic_id` and `post_id` as plain integer columns and only adds an index on `embed_url`; it does not add any DB foreign-key constraints (nor any ON DELETE cascade behavior). In the model, `TopicEmbed` only declares `belongs_to :topic`/`:post`, and the diff does not add corresponding `has_one/has_many ... dependent: :destroy` on `Topic` or `Post`. Therefore, at the database level (and based on what’s shown in the diff), deleting a `Topic` or `Post` can leave orphaned `topic_embeds` rows, which is a real referential-integrity risk introduced by this schema change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No index on topic_id or post_id in create_topic_embeds.rb, causing full table scans for cleanup/lookup joins

adjudication.rationale: The migration `create_topic_embeds` only adds a unique index on `embed_url` and does not index `topic_id` or `post_id`. However, in the diff the code paths shown primarily look up by `embed_url` (`topic_id_for_embed`, `exists?` checks) and do not introduce any required queries/joins on `topic_id`/`post_id` that would be clearly broken or demonstrably problematic without those indexes. The claim about “causing full table scans for cleanup/lookup joins” is a performance speculation rather than a verifiable defect introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No ON DELETE CASCADE or model-level dependent: :destroy from Topic/Post to TopicEmbed, causing orphaned embed rows to accumulate and break EmbedController#best

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new `topic_embeds` table and a `TopicEmbed` model with `belongs_to :topic`/`:post`, but it does not add foreign keys with `ON DELETE CASCADE`. However, the proposed finding also asserts there is no model-level `dependent: :destroy` from `Topic`/`Post` to `TopicEmbed`, which cannot be verified from this diff because the `Topic` model is not shown and no associations are added there. Additionally, the claim that orphaned rows will “break `EmbedController#best`” is speculative: while a stale `topic_id` could cause issues if the topic is deleted, that behavior depends on deletion flows outside this change and is not demonstrably broken by the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: add_cook_method_to_posts.rb:4 hardcodes default: 1 coupled to Post.cook_methods order; inserting a new cook method at position 1 silently changes meaning of all existing rows

adjudication.rationale: The migration `add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1` does hardcode a numeric default, and `Post.cook_methods` is defined as an ordered `Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html)`. However, the proposed issue only materializes if someone later changes the enum ordering (e.g., inserts a new value before `:regular`), which is a hypothetical future change not shown in this diff. In the diff as-is, there’s no demonstrated mismatch or incorrect behavior caused by `default: 1`; it’s a common pattern for integer-backed enums and works with the current two-value ordering.

adjudication_records.issue_text: post_creator.rb:216 accepts any integer for cook_method without validating it is one of Post.cook_methods

adjudication.rationale: In `lib/post_creator.rb` the diff adds `post.cook_method = @opts[:cook_method] if @opts[:cook_method].present?`, which will persist whatever integer/value is provided in `@opts[:cook_method]`. In the same diff, `Post.cook_methods` is defined as an enum with only `:regular` and `:raw_html`, but there is no validation shown on `Post` (e.g., inclusion/enum constraint) to ensure `cook_method` is one of those values. That means callers can store an out-of-range/unknown cook_method, leading to inconsistent behavior (e.g., posts unexpectedly going through the default cooking path) and potentially breaking any code that assumes the value is within the enum.

adjudication_records.issue_text: SHA in topic_embed.rb:14-15 includes localizable footer text, so changing locale strings marks every unchanged article as changed and triggers re-imports/re-cooks

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicEmbed.import`, it mutates `contents` by appending a localized footer (`I18n.t('embed.imported_from', ...)`) and then computes `content_sha1 = Digest::SHA1.hexdigest(contents)`. Because the SHA is computed *after* adding localizable text, a change to the translation (or current locale) will change the SHA even if the upstream article content is identical. On the next poll/import for the same `embed_url`, `content_sha1 != embed.content_sha1` will be true and the code will unnecessarily revise the post and update the SHA.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicEmbed.create! in topic_embed.rb:21-27 not wrapped in rescue RecordNotUnique, causing race condition between pollers to surface as 500

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicEmbed.import`, it does a read-then-create pattern: `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and, if blank, later `TopicEmbed.create!` inside a transaction. The migration adds `add_index :topic_embeds, :embed_url, unique: true`, so concurrent workers/pollers importing the same URL can both observe `embed.blank?` and then race on `create!`, causing an `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique` exception. There is no rescue/handling in this method (or callers like `Jobs::PollFeed` / `TopicRetriever`) shown in the diff, so this would surface as a job failure/500 rather than being gracefully handled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: poll_feed.rb:32 processes every feed item with no LIMIT or upper bound, creating hundreds of topics in a single Sidekiq job on hourly schedule

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, `poll_feed` does `rss.items.each` over the entire parsed feed with no cap, batching, or pagination. For any feed that returns a large item list, a single hourly Sidekiq execution can attempt to import every item in one run (calling `TopicEmbed.import` per item, which may create new topics for unseen URLs). While `TopicEmbed.import` prevents duplicates for already-imported URLs, the job is still unbounded in how many items it will process/create in a single run.

adjudication_records.issue_text: poll_feed.rb:34 calls nil.scrub when i.content is nil (common for RSS items with only description/summary), raising NoMethodError and aborting entire poll
matched_golden_ids: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same root problem: calling `scrub` on `i.content` can raise a NoMethodError when `i.content` is nil, which is common in RSS items that only provide description/summary. This matches the golden issue about missing `content` and needing a fallback (e.g., to description) to avoid crashes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: poll_feed.rb:17 sets retry: false with no per-item isolation, so transient failures silently drop the whole polling cycle with no alert

adjudication.rationale: The diff does set `sidekiq_options retry: false` in `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, and the job does not rescue exceptions around `open(...)`, `SimpleRSS.parse`, or per-item processing, so a single exception would abort that run. However, calling this a definite defect is not verifiable from the diff: disabling retries can be an intentional choice for scheduled polling jobs (it will run again on the next schedule anyway), and the claim that failures are “silently” dropped “with no alert” depends on external logging/monitoring not shown here. This is more of a design/reliability suggestion than a clear bug introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_retriever.rb:35-37 calls Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) synchronously inside a background job, re-fetching and re-importing entire RSS feed on every user visit to un-embedded page

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb, perform_retrieve unconditionally does `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true, before falling back to HTTP fetch. PollFeed#poll_feed (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb) fetches and parses the configured feed URL and iterates through *all* items, calling `TopicEmbed.import` for each, which can create/update topics/posts. TopicRetriever is invoked from the `retrieve_topic` background job (app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb), which is enqueued by EmbedController when an embed for the requested URL is missing. Therefore, each missing-embed request can synchronously trigger a full feed poll/import in that job (subject only to the per-URL 60s throttle), which is a real performance/side-effect problem present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: feed_key defined but never used in poll_feed.rb:20-22 (dead code); Last-Modified/ETag caching not implemented

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, the method `feed_key` is defined (computing a Redis key based on the feed URL) but nothing in this diff calls `feed_key` or otherwise uses that value. `poll_feed` directly does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` with no conditional GET logic, so the suggested caching via Last-Modified/ETag (implied by `feed_key`) is not implemented here. The "dead code" part is directly verifiable from the diff; the caching remark is accurate as an observation but more of a missing-feature note than a bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No rate limiting in embed_controller.rb:13-17; job enqueue itself is unbounded so flood of requests for distinct URLs enqueues flood of fetch jobs

adjudication.rationale: In EmbedController#best, when no TopicEmbed exists for the given embed_url, it unconditionally enqueues Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ..., embed_url: embed_url) on every request. While TopicRetriever has a 60-second throttle, it is keyed by the full embed_url string ("retrieved:#{@embed_url}"), so a flood of requests with distinct embed_url values (all on the allowed embeddable_host) will bypass the throttle and enqueue/execute an unbounded number of jobs and remote fetches. The referer check is only a header comparison and can be spoofed by a non-browser client, so it does not reliably prevent such flooding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: best.html.erb:12 calls post.user.small_avatar_url and post.user.username without nil guard, causing NoMethodError when author is deleted

adjudication.rationale: The new view `app/views/embed/best.html.erb` does call `post.user.small_avatar_url` and `post.user.username` without a nil check. However, the diff does not establish that `post.user` can be nil in this context: `@topic_view.posts` comes from `TopicView`, and nothing in the introduced code creates posts without users or nullifies user associations. In typical Discourse/Rails setups, posts require a user and user deletion is handled without making `post.user` nil (e.g., anonymization or retaining a deleted user record). Therefore the finding relies on speculation about behavior not shown/guaranteed by this diff rather than a verifiable defect introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: absolutize_urls in topic_embed.rb:60-66 only rewrites URLs starting with '/', missing protocol-relative URLs (//host/path), relative paths without leading slash, and ../ paths

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls, both the anchor and image rewrites only run when the URL starts with '/' (e.g., `href.start_with?('/')`). The comment above the method says it converts “any relative URLs to absolute,” but the implementation does not handle other common relative forms such as `//cdn.example.com/path` (protocol-relative), `path/page.html` (relative without leading slash), or `../up/path` (parent-relative). That will leave those URLs unmodified in imported HTML, causing broken links/images in the rendered embedded/imported content.

adjudication_records.issue_text: skip_validations: true and bypass_rate_limiter: true on imported posts (post_revisor.rb:85, topic_embed.rb:22) bypasses post-length and spam validations

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly bypasses validations and rate limiting for imported/updated embedded posts. In `TopicEmbed.import`, new posts are created via `PostCreator.new(..., skip_validations: true, cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html])`, which (by design) skips model validations that would normally enforce constraints like minimum/maximum length and other validation-based checks. For updates, `TopicEmbed.import` calls `PostRevisor#revise!` with `skip_validations: true, bypass_rate_limiter: true`, and the diff modifies `PostRevisor` to honor this by saving with `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])`, ensuring validations are actually skipped. Thus the finding is directly supported by the diff: imported content can bypass validation-based safeguards (including length-related ones) and rate limiting.

adjudication_records.issue_text: --category option removed from disqus.thor:114-149, silently forcing all Disqus-imported topics into default category (regression)

adjudication.rationale: In `lib/tasks/disqus.thor`, the `--category` option and the logic that resolved `category_id` and passed `category: category_id` into `PostCreator` were removed. The new path uses `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`, and `TopicEmbed.import_remote`/`.import` create the topic via `PostCreator.new(... )` without any `category` parameter. So Disqus imports no longer have any way (in this diff) to target a chosen category and will fall back to whatever the default category behavior is (likely Uncategorized). The finding’s “silently” wording is slightly overstated because the CLI option is removed (Thor would reject it), but the underlying regression (loss of category selection, defaulting category) is real and verifiable in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: create_top_topics.rb:3 adds force: true to already-shipped migration, dropping top_topics table and data on replay
create_topic_embeds.rb:4 uses force: true which drops pre-existing topic_embeds data without warning if migration is replayed

adjudication.rationale: The new migration `20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb` creates the table with `create_table :topic_embeds, force: true`. In Rails, `force: true` will drop the table first if it already exists, which can silently delete any pre-existing `topic_embeds` data when the migration is run in an environment where the table exists (e.g., a partially-applied migration, manual table creation, or re-running migrations). This is a real data-loss risk introduced by the diff and is generally unnecessary for a normal migration.

adjudication_records.issue_text: best.html.erb:6 uses `<%- end if %>` which is a syntax error; should be `<%- end %>`
matched_golden_ids: The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both comments flag the same underlying issue: using `end if` to close an ERB/Ruby `if` block is invalid syntax and should be replaced with a plain `end`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embeddable_host in site_settings.yml:353-357 has no validation that it is a bare host, causing silent mis-comparison if admin enters scheme/path/trailing slash

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `embeddable_host` as a plain string site setting (config/site_settings.yml) and then uses it in strict equality checks against `URI(...).host` in both `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` and `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` (e.g., `URI(@embed_url).host` and `URI(request.referer||'').host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host`). `URI(...).host` returns only the bare host (e.g., `example.com`), so if an admin enters a value containing a scheme/path/trailing slash (e.g., `https://example.com/`), the comparison will fail and embedding/retrieval will be rejected. No normalization/validation is introduced in the diff to prevent or correct such values, so this is a real, verifiable correctness/configuration defect introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: poll_feed.rb:23 runs User.where(username_lower: ...) query each poll cycle; verify username_lower index exists or cache resolved user id

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` which executes `User.where(username_lower: SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase).first` each time the scheduled job runs. While that statement is present, the proposed finding frames it as a performance defect requiring an index or caching; whether `username_lower` is indexed (or whether this query is problematic at all given the job runs hourly and only does a single lookup) cannot be verified from the diff. This is a speculative optimization suggestion rather than a clear bug/security/correctness issue introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_embed.rb:75 uses pluck(:topic_id).first which could be pluck_first(:topic_id) to avoid building an array

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed the code is `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: embed_url).pluck(:topic_id).first`. This will return an array then take the first element, but `embed_url` is indexed unique in the migration (`add_index :topic_embeds, :embed_url, unique: true`), so it will pluck at most one value anyway—no meaningful defect or inefficiency is introduced by the diff. Also `pluck_first` is not a standard Rails 4 API, so the suggested change is at best a style/micro-optimization and may not even be available.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Whitespace-only changes in unrelated pre-existing migration file (20131210181901_migrate_word_counts.rb) shouldn't be in this PR

adjudication.rationale: The diff does include a non-functional formatting change in an existing migration (20131210181901_migrate_word_counts.rb): it removes trailing whitespace on a blank line and also changes the file’s EOF newline status (now shows "No newline at end of file"). However, this is not a bug/security/correctness defect introduced by the PR; it’s a process/style concern about unrelated whitespace-only changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Adding force: true to unrelated already-applied migration (20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb) is destructive and unrelated to PR's goal

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes an existing migration `20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb` from `create_table :top_topics do |t|` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true do |t|`. In Rails, `force: true` drops the table if it already exists before creating it, which is inherently destructive if this migration is ever re-run (e.g., in a recreated environment, a partially migrated DB, or via `db:migrate:redo`). Also, modifying an old migration is unrelated to the embedding/feed feature changes and can introduce unexpected data loss for anyone reapplying migrations from scratch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Disqus thor task removes :category option and changes import semantics (TopicEmbed.import_remote instead of permalink-only post), silently removing a user-facing feature unrelated to PR intent

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly removes the `:category` Thor option from `lib/tasks/disqus.thor` and deletes the logic that looked up `category_id` and passed it into `PostCreator` (`category: category_id`). The import path is changed to `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`, which does not accept or set a category, so callers can no longer control the category for imported Disqus threads. This is a concrete behavior change/regression in the Disqus import task.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unrelated whitespace change in post_revisor.rb bundled with behavior change to revise!

adjudication.rationale: In lib/post_revisor.rb the diff includes (1) removal of a blank line after `return false if not should_revise?` and (2) a functional change from `@post.save` to `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])`. The whitespace removal is incidental, but it does not introduce a bug/security/correctness defect—it's a style/review-hygiene nit about bundling unrelated formatting with a behavior change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Embed.js origin validation uses substring matching (indexOf) instead of strict origin comparison (new URL(discourseUrl).origin === e.origin), making it brittle and insecure
TopicEmbed import interpolates URL directly into HTML without escaping, allowing XSS via URLs containing single quotes

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicEmbed.import`, the code appends `"#{url}"` directly into `contents` without HTML-escaping `url`. The only validation is `url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, which does not prevent single quotes or other HTML-breaking characters in the URL path/query (e.g. `http://host/' onmouseover='alert(1)`). Because imported posts are created with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, `Post#cook` returns `raw` unchanged, and the embed view renders it via `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, this becomes a verifiable XSS vector if an attacker can influence the feed item link/id or embed URL content.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Post.rb cook method for raw_html bypasses Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook), so plugins relying on that filter silently won't run for RSS-imported posts

adjudication.rationale: In `Post#cook`, the diff adds an early return: `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. This happens before the existing call to `Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...)`, so for `raw_html` posts (set during RSS/feed import via `PostCreator` in `TopicEmbed.import`), the `:after_post_cook` plugin filter will never run. That is a concrete behavioral change that can break plugins relying on that hook for all posts.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PollFeed job calls CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub) without guarding for nil i.content, causing NoMethodError and killing the feed poll for entries without content

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the code does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`. If a feed item lacks a `content` field (which is plausible across RSS/Atom variants and SimpleRSS mappings), `i.content` will be `nil`, and calling `.scrub` on `nil` raises `NoMethodError`, aborting the job while iterating `rss.items`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PollFeed uses open() with no timeout, size cap, redirect limit, or error handling; failures silently no-op due to retry: false

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the job does `rss = SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` (via `open-uri`) with no explicit `open_timeout`/`read_timeout`, no content-length/size limiting, and no `rescue` around network/parse failures. This can cause the scheduled job to hang a Sidekiq worker on slow/unresponsive endpoints or to raise exceptions on transient failures. Additionally, `sidekiq_options retry: false` means failures will not be retried automatically (though they would still error/log rather than “silently” no-op).

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicEmbed import_remote uses open(url).read with no timeout, max-size limit, or rescue, causing unhandled exceptions in RetrieveTopic job

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, the code does `open(url).read` (open-uri) with no timeout options and no exception handling. Network failures (DNS, connection refused, SSL errors, HTTP errors, long hangs) will raise exceptions from `open`/`read` and they are not rescued in `import_remote`, `TopicRetriever#fetch_http`, or `Jobs::RetrieveTopic#execute`, so the `RetrieveTopic` job can error out due to unhandled exceptions introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EmbedController referer validation is bypassable (referer can be spoofed) and has implicit behavior with blank referer and duplicated error handling

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`, access is controlled by comparing `URI(request.referer || '').host` to `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` and raising on mismatch. The `Referer` header is client-supplied and can be spoofed by a non-browser client, so this check is not a robust security boundary (it can be bypassed by sending a forged Referer). The blank-referer path also implicitly falls into the same mismatch case (URI('').host => nil), and the rescue re-raises the same “invalid referer host” error, but the core issue is that the validation relies on a spoofable header.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Embed layout postMessage uses request.referer as targetOrigin, which becomes empty string when referer is blank, preventing message delivery and breaking embed resizing

adjudication.rationale: The layout does call `parent.postMessage(..., '<%= request.referer %>')`, but the claim that this “becomes empty string when referer is blank” and breaks resizing is not verifiable here because `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` rejects requests with a missing referer (`URI(request.referer || '').host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host`), so the embed pages won’t render in the no-referer case. (There may be a separate issue that `targetOrigin` should be an origin, not a full referer URL, but that’s not what the finding asserts.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: Best.html.erb renders raw post.cooked without sanitization, allowing script execution from imported RSS/Readability content inside the same-origin embed iframe

adjudication.rationale: Yes. `app/views/embed/best.html.erb` renders `post.cooked` via `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. In this diff, `Post#cook` was changed to return `raw` verbatim when `cook_method == :raw_html`, explicitly skipping the normal rendering/sanitization pipeline. `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` from RSS (`PollFeed` uses `SimpleRSS` content with only `CGI.unescapeHTML(...).scrub`) and from remote HTML (`TopicEmbed.import_remote` uses Readability output). Because `raw_html` bypasses cooking and the view outputs it unescaped, any `<script>` (or other executable HTML) present in imported feed content would be served directly to browsers and can execute within the Discourse-served iframe.

adjudication_records.issue_text: New files (embed.css.scss, loading.html.erb, embed.html.erb, topic_retriever.rb) are missing trailing newline, conflicting with repo conventions

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly marks several files with `\ No newline at end of file` (e.g., `app/assets/stylesheets/embed.css.scss`, `app/views/embed/loading.html.erb`, `app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb`, `lib/topic_retriever.rb`, etc.), so the observation is verifiable. However, this is a formatting/convention issue rather than a bug, security issue, or correctness defect introduced by the change, and the diff does not show an enforced repo rule that would make it a functional problem.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicRetriever spec stubs embeddable_host to nil but actually exercises host-mismatch path rather than a dedicated host-not-set path, making test name/intent misleading

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?`, the logic is simply `SiteSetting.embeddable_host != URI(@embed_url).host`. If `embeddable_host` is `nil`, that comparison evaluates to `true`, so `perform_retrieve` is correctly skipped. There is no separate “host-not-set” branch in the implementation, so the spec is not accidentally missing a distinct path—it is testing the actual behavior for a nil setting. The finding is therefore more about test naming nuance than a verifiable defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EmbedController spec success context would crash on @topic_view.posts because TopicView.new is stubbed to return nil, so it doesn't actually validate the success path it claims

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, `@topic_view` is only used by the view template; the controller action itself does not call `@topic_view.posts`. In the spec, `TopicView.expects(:new).with(...)` sets an expectation and (unless `.returns(...)` is added) will return `nil`, so `@topic_view` would indeed be `nil` during rendering. However, RSpec controller specs typically do **not** render views unless `render_views` is enabled, so this does not “crash” the spec as written, and the diff does not show `render_views`. The finding’s claim of a crash is therefore not verifiably true from the diff (though the test is only checking that `TopicView.new` was called, not that the template works).
